newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian banks allowed to lend expat funds locally.
newsitem.headline: Indian banks allowed to lend expat funds locally.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday said banks will be allowed to lend expatriate Indian deposits under the FCNRB scheme to domestic borrowers.
FCNRB refers to the foreign currency non-resident (bank) account scheme held by expatriate Indians in foreign currency.

"With a view to giving greater flexibility to borrowers engaged in productive activities of the economy, banks will be permitted to provide foreign currency denominated loans to their customers under which foreign exchange risk is borne by the borrowers for meeting either their foreign currency or rupee requirements, subject to the following conditions," RBI said.
- The resource base for such loans would consist of FCNR(B) scheme. Banks will not, however, be permitted to fund a foreign currency loan through a buy-sell swap.
- The purpose, tenor and interest rates on these loans may be decided by the banks, within the prudential framework and the credit monitoring guidelines in force.

- Personal loans and loans for consumer durables, etc., should not be provided under this scheme, since the objective is to provide for genuine credit requirements of productive sectors in the economy.
Detailed operating instructions would be issued separately, RBI said.
